thread_analysis.thread_summary: SORD (contact Hiroyuki Takahashi, Product Center PC Development Group), an existing Allion HDMI compliance customer, reaches out via Hsiaoting Huang and Yukihiro Nakano about Bluetooth certification for a PC product line implementing an Intel M.2 Bluetooth module (already 技適-certified) across multiple memory/storage model variants. Itsuo Sakai drafts the response (sent under Nakano's name) addressing both a registration-mechanics question and a general service-scope question, in the same email exchange.
all_questions_found: Can a PC series with multiple model numbers sharing an identical Bluetooth module be registered as a single bulk certification? (see thread_0245_case_01)
What does Allion's Bluetooth certification 'consulting' support actually include, beyond QDID testing and reporting? (see thread_0245_case_02)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Bulk model coverage for a Bluetooth-identical product series is achieved via free derivative-model Product List additions to a single base registration, not a true wildcard/bulk registration mechanism (which SIG does not allow). Allion's full service scope spans quote-stage test determination, RF/RF PHY test modification guidance, profile test sample requirements, fail-item remediation advice, proxy registration with consistency-check troubleshooting, and post-registration audit support.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Both answers follow the principle of translating an abstract customer question (bulk registration possibility; what does consulting mean) into the specific, concrete mechanism or lifecycle stages that actually apply, rather than giving a generic yes/no or vague description.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0245_case_01 and thread_0245_case_02 for the specific risks of each question.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For prospective customers new to Bluetooth certification (even if experienced with adjacent compliance programs like HDMI), proactively walk through the full engagement lifecycle and the free derivative-model registration mechanism early, since these are the two areas most likely to be misunderstood by someone unfamiliar with Bluetooth SIG-specific registration rules.
